info.title: qv
info.description: Command-line tools for Quest Viva: play text adventure games in the terminal, or drive them from another program or an AI agent.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Find problems in a game's scripts without playing it, exiting non-zero if there are any, for example in CI

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the problems as JSON, for programs

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

arguments.name: GAME
arguments.description: The game to check: an .aslx or .quest file

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Run an MCP server over stdio whose tools play a game, for AI agents

options.name: --seed
options.description: Seed the game's random numbers, so the same commands give the same results

options.name: --text-only
options.description: Give the agent only the game's text, without the exits a browser player sees in the compass

options.name: --debug-tools
options.description: Also offer tools for debugging and fixing a game, which reach past what a player can do, such as evaluate, check and docs

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

arguments.name: GAME
arguments.description: The game to serve. Without one, the agent loads games with start_game

commands.name: play
commands.description: Play a game in the terminal

options.name: --seed
options.description: Seed the game's random numbers, so the same commands give the same results

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

arguments.name: GAME
arguments.description: The game to play: a .quest or .aslx file, or an .asl or .cas file from Quest 4 or earlier

commands.name: preview
commands.description: Play a game in your browser, served by qv on this computer only, reloading it when its files change

options.name: --port
options.description: The port to serve on. By default, a free one

options.name: --seed
options.description: Seed the game's random numbers, so the same commands give the same results

options.name: --player
options.description: Serve the WasmPlayer bundle in this folder instead of the one built into qv

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

arguments.name: GAME
arguments.description: The game to preview: usually an .aslx file, but any game the player can play

commands.name: publish
commands.description: Publish a game, with the files in its folder, after checking it for problems

options.name: --format
options.description: What to make, as the Editor's Publish does: quest, a .quest package; html, one web page that loads the player from jsDelivr (a released qv only); or zip, the page and the player for any web host [default: quest]

options.name: --output
options.description: Where to write it. By default, beside the game: game.aslx makes game.quest, game.html or game-html.zip

options.name: --force
options.description: Publish even if qv check finds problems in the game

options.name: --player
options.description: For --format zip, use the WasmPlayer bundle in this folder instead of the one built into qv

options.name: --cdn-version
options.description: For --format html, load the player from jsDelivr at this published version instead of qv's own

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

arguments.name: GAME
arguments.description: The game to publish: an .aslx file

commands.name: serve
commands.description: Play a game over a JSON-lines protocol on stdin/stdout, for programs to drive

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

commands.name: walkthrough
commands.description: Run a game's built-in walkthroughs, exiting non-zero if any fails, for example in CI

options.name: --seed
options.description: Seed the game's random numbers (default 1234, so every run gives the same results)

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print only whether each walkthrough passed, not its transcript

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

arguments.name: GAME
arguments.description: The game to play: a .quest or .aslx file, or an .asl or .cas file from Quest 4 or earlier

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The walkthrough to run. Without one, every walkthrough runs, each from a fresh start

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information
